title_en: Lü Xuewen — disruption of computer information system case

full_text_en:
Lü Xuewen — crime of damaging computer information system

Procuratorial Authority: People's Procuratorate of Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Defendant: Lü Xuewen, male, 25 years old, born in Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, senior high school education, unemployed, arrested on May 5, 1998.

Defense Counsel: Li Zhibo and Liao Shifei, lawyers from Guangdong Huanyu Commercial Law Firm.

The People's Procuratorate of Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, initiated a public prosecution against the defendant Lü Xuewen before the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court on the charge of damaging a computer information system.

The indictment alleged: The defendant Lü Xuewen intruded into the Guangzhou host of the China Public Multimedia Communication Network (hereinafter referred to as the "Guangzhou host") and the Blue Sky BBS host, and carried out a series of illegal operations including modification, addition, and deletion. His conduct violated the provisions of Article 286, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, constituting the crime of damaging a computer information system, and he should be punished in accordance with the law.

The defendant Lü Xuewen argued in court: I modified the root (highest authority) password of the Guangzhou host with the consent of the network administrator of that host, and it was not an illegal modification. My purpose in intruding into the Guangzhou host and the Blue Sky host was to test whether the method of attempting to enter others' hosts was feasible, and to learn how to ensure network security from it. I was not engaged in destructive activities.

Lü Xuewen's defense counsel argued: The defendant Lü Xuewen did not damage the functions, data, or application programs of the computer information system. His intrusion did not render the computer information system unable to operate normally and did not produce serious consequences. The charges in the indictment cannot be established, and Lü Xuewen should be acquitted.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court found through trial:

In April 1997, the defendant Lü Xuewen joined a domestic hacker organization. From January to February 1998, Lü Xuewen used his laptop computer, stole the accounts of Zou, Wang, He, and Zhu, and used two other illegal accounts to log on to the internet from the multimedia reading room of the Zhongshan Library in Guangdong Province and from his own home. He attacked the Guangzhou host using methods obtained from the internet. After successfully intruding into the host system and obtaining the highest authority, Lü Xuewen illegally created two accounts with the highest authority and one ordinary user account in order to permanently retain control of the host system. During this period, from February 2 to 27, Lü Xuewen repeatedly used the account "gzlittle" to log on and intrude into the Guangzhou host, carrying out a series of operations including modifying, adding, and deleting certain files in the host system. He illegally created three accounts, "gzfifa," "gzmicro," and "gzasia," and gave them to Yuan Mou (separately dealt with) for use, and also illegally installed and debugged network security monitoring software, which was unsuccessful. On February 25 and 26, Lü Xuewen illegally modified the root password of the Guangzhou host system three times, causing the highest authority password of the host system to fail three times, resulting in the host system's management being out of control for approximately 15 hours. When the network administrator of the Guangzhou host first discovered that he could not enter the superuser state of the host for management using his own set root password, Lü Xuewen went online and actively requested to talk to the network administrator, asking the administrator if he had lost the password and claiming that he could change it back. When the administrator asked him whether he had changed the password set by the administrator, Lü Xuewen flatly denied it. Under these circumstances, in order to enter and operate the host, the administrator had to agree to Lü Xuewen's "help" to change the password back. Lü Xuewen then informed the administrator that the root password had been changed to "root123." After testing and confirming that the password "root123" was usable, the administrator, for security reasons, changed "root123" to another password. However, the administrator soon discovered that this newly changed password had been changed back to "root123," known only to Lü Xuewen and the administrator. On the afternoon of February 26, after the Guangzhou host adopted measures to block ordinary users from logging into the host, only Lü Xuewen could still log in by illegal means. During this period, the root password of the host failed a third time, and Lü Xuewen again actively talked to the administrator. Although he again denied modifying the host's password, he told the administrator the new root password that could be used to enter the host. After carrying out the intrusion, Lü Xuewen deleted the records of the accounts he used and also changed the dial-up phone numbers in the dial-up information file to 12345678 or 00000000 to cover up his intrusion.

In addition, on February 12, 1998, the defendant Lü Xuewen also attacked the Blue Sky BBS host using the .Lss program and the obtained password. After obtaining the highest authority of that host, he upgraded the LP account to a highest authority user account in order to permanently retain the highest authority of that host.

The above facts are confirmed by material evidence such as Lü Xuewen's tools of crime, documentary evidence such as photographs of the crime scenes, communication records, and file records, as well as expert conclusions, witness testimony, and other evidence.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court held:

As computer information systems become increasingly integrated into all areas of social life, crimes targeting computer information systems are also increasing, becoming a factor of social instability. Punishing such criminal activities in accordance with the law has become an important task of criminal law.

Article 7 of the "Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Computer Information System Security," promulgated by the State Council on February 18, 1994, stipulates: "No organization or individual may use computer information systems to engage in activities harmful to the interests of the state, collective interests, or the legitimate interests of citizens, nor may they endanger the security of computer information systems." The defendant Lü Xuewen violated this provision by using his knowledge to intrude into the information systems of the Guangzhou host and the Blue Sky BBS host, obtaining the highest authority to control the systems, and carrying out three types of destructive acts: adding accounts with the highest authority and ordinary accounts; deleting, modifying, and monitoring data stored, processed, or transmitted by the Guangzhou host; and modifying the highest authority password of the Guangzhou host three times.

Article 286, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Whoever, in violation of state regulations, deletes, modifies, adds to, or interferes with the functions of a computer information system, thereby causing the computer information system to be unable to operate normally, if the consequences are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention; if the consequences are especially serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years." Paragraph 2 provides: "Whoever, in violation of state regulations, deletes, modifies, or adds to the data or application programs stored, processed, or transmitted in a computer information system, if the consequences are serious, shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph." Accounts and passwords on a computer information system are part of the functions of the computer information system, as manifested in the form of data. The defendant Lü Xuewen's modification and addition of accounts and passwords on the computer information system violated the provisions of Article 286, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law. Furthermore, Lü Xuewen's installation and debugging of network security monitoring software in the Guangzhou host system constituted the deletion, modification, and addition of application programs stored, processed, or transmitted in the computer information system, violating the provisions of Article 286, Paragraph 2. Lü Xuewen's conduct has endangered the security of the computer information system, resulting in serious consequences of loss of control over the management of the Guangzhou host and its inability to operate normally. His conduct constitutes the crime of damaging a computer information system, and he should be punished according to law. The personal property he used for the crime shall be confiscated and turned over to the state treasury in accordance with Article 64 of the Criminal Law.

After intruding into the Guangzhou host, the defendant Lü Xuewen became the only person other than the network administrator to obtain the highest authority over the host. Although Lü Xuewen flatly denied privately modifying the root password of the Guangzhou host, the circumstance that after the network administrator changed the password "root123," told to him by Lü Xuewen, to another password, and this newly set password was immediately changed back to "root123," known only to him and Lü Xuewen, is sufficient to confirm that no one other than Lü Xuewen could have modified the password.

The defendant Lü Xuewen mastered and modified the password of the Guangzhou host, rendering even the network administrator unable to enter the host system for management work. Under these circumstances, Lü Xuewen told the administrator the password he had modified, enabling the administrator to continue operating the host. This act only mitigated the harmful consequences of the crime; it did not change the criminal nature of the conduct, nor did it constitute providing assistance to the network administrator.

Regardless of the purpose, illegally entering a computer information system and performing operations such as deletion and modification, thereby causing the computer information system to be unable to operate normally with serious consequences, constitutes a criminal act as defined by the Criminal Law. The opinions of the defendant Lü Xuewen and his defense counsel that the modification of the password was with the consent of the network administrator, that the entry into the information system was for the purpose of learning, and that there was no destruction of the information system, and therefore the conduct does not constitute a crime, cannot be sustained.

In conclusion, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on August 19, 1999:

1. The defendant Lü Xuewen is convicted of the crime of damaging a computer information system and is sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year and six months;

2. The laptop computer (one unit) seized as Lü Xuewen's tool for committing the crime is confiscated and turned over to the state treasury.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, the defendant Lü Xuewen did not appeal, and the People's Procuratorate did not protest.
